title: I built Battle Tanks - a Battle City inspired low poly shooter with power-ups
author: Labby92
selftext:
I made **Battle Tanks**, a free browser-based arena shooter inspired by Battle City.

You clear short waves of enemy tanks, choose a power-up after each one, and build a loadout around different weapon and upgrade combinations. It supports solo play and same-keyboard local co-op.

I built most of it with Codex 5.4, then used 5.6 later in development. The stack is TypeScript and Three.js, using WebGPU where available with a WebGL fallback. Everything runs client-side.

The game is live on itch.io: [https://montalesidev.itch.io/battle-tanks](https://montalesidev.itch.io/battle-tanks)

The balance still needs work, but I’ve been happy with it in my own playthroughs. If you try it, share your high score and favorite loadout. I’d like to know what feels strong, weak, or just fun to use.

replies.author: Labby92
replies.body: Thanks, I quickly put it up on itch. I’ll improve it over the coming days

replies.author: promptling
replies.body: The fastest home page test is to show it to five people for ten seconds, hide it, then ask what the game is, whether it runs in the browser, and what they would click next. If those answers are fuzzy, lead with one clear gameplay clip and one Play button before anything else. Full disclosure, I am building [Patchloop](https://patchloop.io/) for agentically built games in progress and focused feedback loops. Battle Tanks could be a good fit for a before and after test as you update it.

comments.author: xendelaar
comments.body: I like it. Wouldnt it be better to have a rotating turret? Or would that break the gameplay in several ways?

replies.author: Labby92
replies.body: Thank you! I simply wanted to retain the feel of the original Battle City and put a twist on it with some cooler power-up. That’s why I kept the movement this way.
